title: Before You Buy an AI Document Assistant
content:
If your AI assistant can't show WHERE its answer came from, don't put it in front of your team.
Here are four questions to ask before you buy or build one.
Every business has the same pain.
Policies, contracts, product manuals, SOPs, spread across hundreds of files.
So the idea of asking an AI is very attractive.
But an assistant that sounds confident and is wrong is more dangerous than no assistant at all.
Question ONE. Does every answer show its source?
Not just the file name. The exact page or section.
Your team should be able to click and check in five seconds.
If they can't check it, they can't trust it.
Question TWO. Can it say "I don't know"?
Ask it something that is NOT in your documents.
A good assistant admits it. A weak one invents an answer.
This single test tells you more than any sales demo.
Now, the question most buyers forget.
And it is the one that can get you into real trouble.
Question THREE. Who can see what?
Imagine an intern asks about salaries, and the assistant answers from an HR file.
The assistant must respect the same access rules as your shared drive.
Security is not a feature you add later.
Question FOUR. How is it tested?
Ask for a simple test set, twenty or thirty real questions with known answers.
Check the answer and the source for each one.
Then repeat that test every time the documents or the model change.
Here's my take... these four checks are not fancy.
But they decide whether your team uses the tool for a week, or for years.
Start with one department and one folder of documents.
Measure how much search time it saves before you roll it out wider.
